claims.statement: categorize_pending always pairs transfers first, categorizes pending rows, saves results, then calls link_loans, including when the pending list is empty or jev is skipped.
A missing TYPESAFE_API_KEY forces a rules-only jev skip: pairing and system rules still run, unmatched rows stay category_source none, and the summary reports that jev was skipped.

Production runs are started by POST /imports and POST /categorize/run as a background task, or synchronously by finance categorize and finance import. The HTTP run accepts all to re-categorize non-user rows; the CLI also has --rules-only.
Pending rows are those with category_source none, or every non-user source when include_all is set, ordered by booked_at then id. User-labelled rows are never loaded into the cascade.

Inside categorize, a row with transfer_pair_id is labelled own_accounts from a rule before any system rule; otherwise the first matching categorize rule wins. Those rows never call jev and are always returned, even when jev is None.

pair_transfers links opposite equal amounts on different accounts whose description matches transfer_pattern within transfer_window_days, preferring globally nearest dates, one-to-one. Same account, unequal amounts, and non-matching text do not pair.

A user-labelled row is a pairing candidate only when its slug is already own_accounts. Pairing links it but does not overwrite that label or insert a rule history row; other paired sides are written as own_accounts with source rule and needs_review false.

Enabled system rules are loaded by name order from the rules table. The first categorize rule whose bank, direction, and case-insensitive field pattern match wins. Refund rules never assign a category.
A matching refund rule makes an incoming row offer expense category leaves to jev instead of income leaves. Other incoming rows still see income plus transfer leaves.

Each unmatched row gets one parallel jev call named categorize with three independent questions: merchant_name Choice over 1-4 word fragments plus none, category Choice over the offered leaves, and is_subscription Noul.

jev state contains bank, bank_concept, merchant_text, amount, and direction, not description_raw. Fragments drop any token containing a digit, so a card number in the raw description never reaches jev.
Merchant resolution runs one row at a time in booking-date then id order. An exact match_key reuses a known merchant without a second jev call, even below the brand threshold.

A new merchant name whose nested-fragment brand confidence is below brand_threshold (default 0.5) is dropped and the row needs review. Confidence equal to 0.5 creates the merchant. The brand gate does not apply to an exact-key hit.

A new name that shares a significant word with known merchants gets a same_merchant jev call. Confidence at or above merge_threshold (default 0.8) reuses the known merchant; at or above merge_suggestion_floor (default 0.5) and below the merge threshold creates a new merchant plus a merge suggestion; below the floor creates a separate merchant.

When merchant defaults are enabled, a resolved merchant's category_slug replaces jev and the source becomes merchant, clearing confidence so the row skips the review threshold. An income default does not apply to money out. Eval disables defaults and uses an empty roster.

A jev category needs review only when its confidence is strictly below category_threshold (default 0.95). A subscription is set only when noul is strictly above subscription_threshold (default 0.7) and the row is an outgoing expense. Equal category confidence is accepted; equal subscription score is not a subscription.
Review lists non-user rows with needs_review, plus pending merge suggestions. Rows still at category_source none are counted as uncategorized rather than as category cards.

link_loans assigns one merchant_source rule merchant to loan_received and loan_payment rows that have no merchant, naming it from the last four digits of a 4-4-2-10 contract number and reusing a merchant already linked to that contract so a renamed loan keeps later instalments.
save preserves a merchant_source rule merchant across re-categorization, so a renamed loan merchant survives an --all rewrite of the loan rule result.

A failed or malformed jev answer omits only that row, logs the transaction id and exception without the description, and leaves the row pending for the next run. Other rows, including pairing and rule rows, are still saved.
save will not overwrite a row whose category_source is already user, and it writes no label history when that update matches zero rows. A user label applied while jev was answering therefore stands.
Background categorization holds a process-local threading lock so queued runs do not overlap, and logs rather than raises if the run fails, so an import is not failed by categorization.
